sentences.en: Wetlands are areas where water covers the soil, or is present either at or near the surface of the soil, for all or part of the year.
sentences.zh: 湿地是这样的区域：一年中的全部或部分时间里，水覆盖着土壤，或者水就处在土壤表面或接近地表的位置。

sentences.en: These are complex ecosystems, rich in unique plant and animal life.
sentences.zh: 湿地是复杂的生态系统，生活着丰富而独特的动植物。

sentences.en: But according to the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWFN), half of the world’s wetlands have disappeared since 1990 — converted or destroyed for commercial development, drainage schemes and the extraction of minerals and peat*.
sentences.zh: 但据世界自然基金会介绍，自1990年以来，全球已有一半湿地消失。为了商业开发、实施排水工程，以及开采矿产和泥炭，人们改变了这些湿地的用途，或将其破坏。

sentences.en: Many of those that remain have been damaged by agricultural pesticides and fertilisers, industrial pollutants, and construction works.
sentences.zh: 剩下的湿地中，也有许多受到农药、化肥、工业污染物和建筑工程的损害。

sentences.en: Throughout history, humans have gathered around wetlands, and their fertile ecosystems have played an important part in human development.
sentences.zh: 纵观历史，人类一直在湿地周边聚居；湿地肥沃的生态系统在人类发展中发挥了重要作用。

sentences.en: Consequently, they are of considerable religious, historical and archaeological value to many communities around the world.
sentences.zh: 因此，对世界上许多社群而言，湿地有着相当重要的宗教、历史和考古价值。

sentences.en: ‘Wetlands directly support the livelihoods and well-being of millions of people,’ says Dr Matthew McCartney, principal researcher and hydrologist at the International Water Management Institute (IWMI).
sentences.zh: “湿地直接维系着数百万人的生计与福祉。”国际水资源管理研究所首席研究员、水文学家马修·麦卡特尼博士说。

sentences.en: ‘In many developing countries, large numbers of people are dependent on wetland agriculture for their livelihoods.’
sentences.zh: “在许多发展中国家，有大量人口依靠湿地农业谋生。”

sentences.en: They also serve a crucial environmental purpose.
sentences.zh: 湿地还发挥着至关重要的环境作用。

sentences.en: ‘Wetlands are one of the key tools in mitigating climate change across the planet,’ says Pieter van Eijk, head of Climate Adaptation at Wetlands International (WI), pointing to their use as buffers that protect coastal areas from sea-level rise and extreme weather events such as hurricanes and flooding.
sentences.zh: 国际湿地组织气候适应部门负责人彼得·范艾克说：“湿地是全球缓解气候变化的重要手段之一。”他指出，湿地可以充当缓冲带，保护沿海地区免受海平面上升以及飓风、洪水等极端天气事件的影响。

sentences.en: Wetland coastal forests provide food and water, as well as shelter from storms, and WI and other agencies are working to restore those forests which have been lost.
sentences.zh: 沿海湿地森林能提供食物和水，还可让人们躲避风暴。国际湿地组织和其他机构正努力恢复已经消失的这类森林。

sentences.en: ‘It can be as simple as planting a few trees per hectare to create shade and substantially change a microclimate,’ he says.
sentences.zh: “做法可以很简单，比如每公顷种上几棵树来提供树荫，就能大幅改变当地的小气候。”他说。

sentences.en: ‘Implementing climate change projects isn’t so much about money.’
sentences.zh: “实施气候变化项目，钱并不是最重要的。”

sentences.en: The world’s wetlands are, unfortunately, rich sources for in-demand commodities, such as palm oil and pulpwood.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，世界各地的湿地也盛产一些需求旺盛的商品，例如棕榈油和造纸用材。

sentences.en: Peatlands — wetlands with a waterlogged organic soil layer — are particularly targeted.
sentences.zh: 泥炭地是有一层浸透水的有机土壤的湿地，尤其容易成为开发目标。

sentences.en: When peatlands are drained for cultivation, they become net carbon emitters instead of active carbon stores, and, according to Marcel Silvius, head of Climate-smart Land-use at WI, this practice causes six per cent of all global carbon emissions.
sentences.zh: 泥炭地一旦排水用于耕种，就会从持续储碳的地方变成碳的净排放源。据国际湿地组织气候智慧型土地利用部门负责人马塞尔·西尔维乌斯介绍，这种做法造成的碳排放占全球碳排放总量的6%。

sentences.en: The clearance of peatlands for planting also increases the risk of forest fires, which release huge amounts of CO₂.
sentences.zh: 为了种植作物而清理泥炭地，还会增加森林火灾的风险，而森林火灾会释放大量二氧化碳。

sentences.en: ‘We’re seeing huge peatland forests with extremely high biodiversity value being lost for a few decades of oil palm revenues,’ says Silvius.
sentences.zh: “我们眼看着大片生物多样性价值极高的泥炭地森林消失，换来的只是几十年的油棕收益。”西尔维乌斯说。

sentences.en: The damage starts when logging companies arrive to clear the trees.
sentences.zh: 破坏从伐木公司进场清除树木时就开始了。

sentences.en: They dig ditches to enter the peat swamps by boat and then float the logs out the same way.
sentences.zh: 他们挖沟渠，以便乘船进入泥炭沼泽，再让原木顺着同样的水路漂运出去。

sentences.en: These are then used to drain water out of the peatlands to allow for the planting of corn, oil palms or pulpwood trees.
sentences.zh: 接着，人们利用这些沟渠排出泥炭地的水，以便种植玉米、油棕或供造纸用的树木。

sentences.en: Once the water has drained away, bacteria and fungi then break down the carbon in the peat and turn it into CO₂ and methane.
sentences.zh: 水一排走，细菌和真菌就开始分解泥炭中的碳，把它转化成二氧化碳和甲烷。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the remainder of the solid matter in the peat starts to move downwards, in a process known as subsidence**.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，泥炭中剩下的固态物质开始向下移动，这个过程称为地面沉降。

sentences.en: Peat comprises 90 per cent water, so this is one of the most alarming consequences of peatland clearances.
sentences.zh: 泥炭的含水量达90%，所以地面沉降是清理泥炭地最令人担忧的后果之一。

sentences.en: ‘In the tropics, peat subsides at about four centimetres a year, so within half a century, very large landscapes on Sumatra and Borneo will become flooded as the peat drops below water level,’ says Silvius.
sentences.zh: “在热带地区，泥炭每年下沉约4厘米。所以不出半个世纪，苏门答腊岛和婆罗洲的大片区域就会因为泥炭降至水面以下而被淹没。”西尔维乌斯说。

sentences.en: ‘It’s a huge catastrophe that’s in preparation.
sentences.zh: “一场巨大的灾难正在酝酿。

sentences.en: Some provinces will lose 40 per cent of their landmass.’
sentences.zh: 有些省份将会失去40%的陆地面积。”

sentences.en: And while these industries affect wetlands in ways that can easily be documented, Dr Dave Tickner of the WWFN believes that more subtle impacts can be even more devastating.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些产业对湿地的影响很容易记录下来，世界自然基金会的戴夫·蒂克纳博士认为，一些不易察觉的影响甚至可能更具破坏性。

sentences.en: ‘Sediment run-off and fertilisers can be pretty invisible,’ says Tickner.
sentences.zh: “随地表径流流失的泥沙和肥料都可能很难察觉。”蒂克纳说。

sentences.en: ‘Over-extraction of water is equally invisible.
sentences.zh: “过度取水也同样难以察觉。

sentences.en: You do get shock stories about rivers running red, or even catching fire, but there’s seldom one big impact that really hurts a wetland.’
sentences.zh: 确实有河水变红甚至起火的骇人报道，但真正伤害湿地的，很少是某一次重大的冲击。”

sentences.en: Tickner does not blame anyone for deliberate damage, however.
sentences.zh: 不过，蒂克纳并没有指责任何人有意破坏湿地。

sentences.en: ‘I’ve worked on wetland issues for 20 years and have never met anybody who wanted to damage a wetland,’ he says.
sentences.zh: “我从事湿地相关工作已有20年，从没遇见过一个存心破坏湿地的人。”他说。

sentences.en: ‘It isn’t something that people generally set out to do.
sentences.zh: “一般说来，人们一开始并没有要破坏湿地的打算。

sentences.en: Quite often, the effects simply come from people trying to make a living.’
sentences.zh: 很多时候，这些影响只是人们设法谋生所带来的结果。”

sentences.en: Silvius also acknowledges the importance of income generation.
sentences.zh: 西尔维乌斯也承认，为当地人创造收入很重要。

sentences.en: ‘It’s not that we just want to restore the biodiversity of wetlands — which we do — but we recognise there’s a need to provide an income for local people.’
sentences.zh: “我们确实想恢复湿地的生物多样性，但我们的目标不止于此。我们也认识到，有必要让当地居民获得收入。”

sentences.en: This approach is supported by IWMI.
sentences.zh: 国际水资源管理研究所也支持这种做法。

sentences.en: ‘The idea is that people in a developing country will only protect wetlands if they value and profit from them,’ says McCartney.
sentences.zh: “我们的看法是，发展中国家的居民只有看重湿地并能从中获益，才会保护湿地。”麦卡特尼说。

sentences.en: ‘For sustainability, it’s essential that local people are involved in wetland planning and decision making and have clear rights to use wetlands.’
sentences.zh: “要让湿地得到可持续利用，关键是让当地居民参与湿地的规划和决策，并让他们拥有明确的湿地使用权。”

sentences.en: The fortunes of wetlands would be improved, Silvius suggests, if more governments recognised their long-term value.
sentences.zh: 西尔维乌斯认为，如果更多政府认识到湿地的长远价值，湿地的处境就会改善。

sentences.en: ‘Different governments have different attitudes,’ he says, and goes on to explain that some countries place a high priority on restoring wetlands, while others still deny the issue.
sentences.zh: “各国政府的态度各不相同。”他接着解释，有些国家把恢复湿地列为优先事项，而另一些国家仍然否认问题的存在。

sentences.en: McCartney is cautiously optimistic, however.
sentences.zh: 不过，麦卡特尼对此持谨慎乐观的态度。

sentences.en: ‘Awareness of the importance of wetlands is growing,’ he says.
sentences.zh: “人们越来越认识到湿地的重要性。”他说。

sentences.en: ‘It’s true that wetland degradation still continues at a rapid pace, but my impression is that things are slowly changing.’
sentences.zh: “湿地的确仍在迅速退化，但在我看来，情况正慢慢改变。”
